But preservation came with a disputed 2006 relocation, resident numbers keep falling, and scholars criticise the artist–resident interaction as 'still too little' — the settlement was saved, but not necessarily its people.
k49.selfDesc: The official site says 'art-and-living coexistence' revitalises Treasure Hill by building art and living together, and admits that 'living' first meant the community's residents but has since widened to all the units and occupants in the settlement; the settlement is formed of 1960s–70s informal buildings, was registered as a historic settlement in 2004, repairs by the Bureau began in late 2006, and over twenty-odd years the Taipei Artist Village and Treasure Hill together have hosted more than 500 creators from over 40 countries. Fu Jen student outlet Vita (on PeoPo, 2023-11-03) records resident participation: a roughly bimonthly 'one dish per household' meal; after the March light festival residents also create in the garden, and a big bamboo cage left from an earlier festival was taken by residents to raise chickens and geese; the 'Treasure Village' shop is run by Auntie Qiuhong with the village's help, serving a set meal on Tuesdays and Thursdays; Chou Ling-chih moved in in 2008 and co-designed the shared garden; early on an elderly veteran demanded artists show a 'residence permit' and waved a cane to drive them off, tourists wandered into homes, and the village used surname signs and stanchions to protect privacy; 19 original households remain. PTS 'Our Island' (a 2007 piece, not re-read this time) is cited by the user as reporting that in 2006 some sixty-odd households moved out but only 16 actually entered transitional housing, with some residents calling it eviction in disguise. Eyes on Place (Liu Ke-chiang, 2021-01-06) notes residents keep declining, that under current rules the housing area could be empty within about a decade, that artist–resident interaction is 'still too little', and that a film-and-video experimental school occupies housing originally reserved for residents but vacated as they left. King's College London scholar Igor Rogelja analyses the preservation as a form of 'museumification': after the city offered three compensation/relocation options in 2006, it cleared the village on 22 Dec 2006 and riot police cleared the rest on 30 Jan 2007; renovated houses were let on 12-year tenancies, and households fell from over 70 before eviction to 21 in 2014 and 19 in 2018, the author arguing this turns residents and artists into a watched 'living diorama'.
k49.pedagogicalInsight: This is the best case for discussing what happens when art moves into a place that still has people living in it and carries historical wounds — and you need both sides. On the positive side it models treating shared living itself as method: the one-dish meal, the shared garden, the corner shop are not an event but a slow way for artists and residents to come into relationship; after the light festival residents create in the garden themselves and take the bamboo cage to raise poultry — a fine example of residents 'taking over' art as life. But the more important teaching material is the cracks: the official site widens 'living' from original residents to all occupants, while scholars note residents keep falling and interaction is 'still too little', and early on a veteran demanded artists show a 'residence permit'. With students you can ask together: when we say 'coexistence', whose 'living' is counted? Does saving the houses mean saving the people? These have no neat answers, which is exactly the case's value. Rogelja's critique makes a sharper prompt for students: when the preserved residents become a watched 'living diorama', who is the preservation really for?
k49.why: Verified: the core facts (an informal settlement saved as a historic settlement, the coexistence model, the three-option 2006 relocation and clearance, a fall from over 70 households to about 19, the museumification dispute) are corroborated by the official site, Rogelja's academic paper citing Taipei City documents, the 2006 Liberty Times report, the Eyes on Place scholar piece and PTS. The specific resident co-creation activities still rest on a single source, as noted.

k48.name: Daxi Daxi (series)
k48.creator: Taoyuan City Cultural Affairs Bureau and the Daxi Wood Art Ecomuseum (hosts); designer Liao Xiao-zi (key visuals for four editions); BIAS Architects (execution, book)
k48.place: Daxi District, Taoyuan — Puji Temple and the old town
k48.year: From 2018 (series; detailed content known for 2022, 2–22 Jul, and 2026, opening 18 Jul)
k48.summary: The birthday procession for Lord Guan at Daxi's Puji Temple was originally a grassroots faith festival (the 24th day of the sixth lunar month, called Daxi people's 'second New Year'). Since 2018 the Daxi Wood Art Ecomuseum has turned it into a festival brand, 'Daxi Daxi', built on 'experience x participation x revival', with designer Liao Xiao-zi making the key visuals for four editions. The 2022 edition brought a pop-up picture book and teaching materials and the 'Wu De Dian' shen-jiang interactive show, and invited the public to join the procession wearing shen-jiang paper hats; the 2026 edition centred on 'festival music', gathering 32 shetou across about 40 events, with nine shetou performing with pop musicians. Temple staff, volunteers, Daxi's many trades and the shetou take part together.
k48.selfDesc: The museum's official page frames Daxi Daxi as preserving and re-presenting a 'century-old intangible cultural asset', using Daxi itself as the stage and drawing residents, shops and audiences into experiential learning; it explains the participants include temple staff, volunteers, Daxi's trades and the shetou — self-organised procession troupes formed by shared trade or locality (e.g. the ox-plough, ink-line and plasterer-boy troupes). VERSE's book panel (2023) notes Daxi Daxi has run since 2018, that BIAS Architects and the museum produced the book, and that Liao Xiao-zi designed the key visuals for four editions, calling it 'a city festival across contemporary design and folk belief'. Marie Claire (2022) records the pop-up book (Liao as art director), the 'Wu De Dian' show (with a 'righteous-steps' learning device), the 'procession with the gods' handing out paper hats, Vitali co-branded sodas, and 'Daxi Daxi' merchandise and amulets. Storm (2026) notes the bureau's 'experience, participation, revival' core and that residents, shetou and shops co-created the curation.
k48.pedagogicalInsight: This case shows how to turn a living local tradition into something outsiders and young people can enter. The point is not that the museum invented anything, but that design and experiential devices turn onlookers into participants — paper hats let the public walk in the procession, a 'righteous-steps' device lets people learn the generals' walk with their bodies, and a picture book and lesson plans let Daxi people learn to tell their own festival as a story. For a teacher, the lesson is: find what the community already does, then design an 'entry point' for taking part, rather than inventing an event from scratch. The shetou are also worth discussing — the unit of participation is an existing group formed by trade or locality, not the individual. One useful tension to raise with students is commercialisation: do Lord-Guan sodas and gift packs bring more people into the festival, or turn belief into consumption? There is no set answer, which makes it good for debate.
k48.why: Verified: the official page and three different outlets (VERSE 2023, Marie Claire 2022, Storm 2026) corroborate the hosts, the 'experience/participation/revival' idea, Liao Xiao-zi's four editions of key visuals and shetou participation. A few details (the 2018 start, 32 shetou / ~40 events) still rest on single sources, as noted.

k47.name: 2022 Mattauw Land Art Festival: A Thousand Names of the Zengwen River
k47.creator: Chief curator Gong Zhuo-jun (龔卓軍); co-curator Luo Jian-yu (羅健毓); advisers Qiu Ru-hua (丘如華) and Zeng Xu-zheng (曾旭正); hosted by the Tainan City Government Cultural Affairs Bureau (per Storm Media; the official site shows the host only as logos); nine sub-projects
k47.place: Zongye Art Center in Mattau, Tainan, plus the Dubar and Dalongtian zones (per the official site) and the Provincial Road 171 area, with partners from the upper to lower Zengwen River; sources name the zones differently
k47.summary: A campaign-style land art festival hosted by the Tainan City Government Cultural Affairs Bureau with the whole Zengwen River as its subject, held October 2022 – January 2023 under the theme 'A Thousand Names of the Zengwen River'. Its long-term goal is 'legal personhood for rivers' and its core is a 'watershed community'. It has nine strands — Small Projects, Water, Bamboo, Sneak Photography, Vegetation, Soil, Farming, Sound and Origins — linking partners from Tsou villages upstream, meandering farm villages midstream and canal-and-fishpond areas downstream, with public-participation activities such as the 'Parliament of All Things' and the 'Little News' news camp. It is the edition before the 2026 festival (K32).
k47.selfDesc: The official site's 'About' page calls it the 'nation's first' land art festival with a whole river as its subject, with the long-term goal of 'legal personhood for rivers' and a 'watershed community' as the core of its action and awareness; it calls on people to 'exchange bodies with bodies' and enter the living worlds of the river. It mentions 'three years of long-term fieldwork' and 'three years of research', lists nine sub-projects and three joint presentations, and says it links partners from Tsou villages upstream, meandering farm villages midstream and canal-and-fishpond areas downstream, promoting public participation and deliberation through the 'Parliament of All Things' and the 'Little News' news camp. Storm Media (2022) calls it 'Taiwan's first art festival focused on river rights', hosted by the Tainan Cultural Affairs Bureau, and says Chiayi County and the Water Resources Agency were invited to sign a watershed governance agreement (the article does not say whether it was signed). The Reporter's Sneak Photography feature records photographers and writers staying long-term along the basin, photographing a Tsou modern hunter, mango growers, 'water keepers' and young people from multicultural families.
k47.pedagogicalInsight: 'A river with a thousand names' makes a good classroom prompt: what do hunters, fruit growers, water keepers and children each call the same stream, and how do they use it? Have students collect the names and water stories of a nearby canal, drain or small river, so the issue grows out of residents' own words rather than the teacher lecturing on water policy. The case also models 'stay first, curate later': the official site mentions three years of research before the exhibition, a reminder that depth of issue comes from time. Note that it is a campaign-style festival whose goal, 'legal personhood for rivers', was set from the start; in class you can ask one more question — where does this stance come from, and may students disagree? Also, the site gives only the names of the 'Parliament of All Things' and 'Little News' camp, not how they are run; check the original organiser's practice before borrowing them rather than guessing a process from the names.
k47.why: The official site (organiser's own account), Storm Media and the Reporter feature agree on the host, chief curator, run dates, zones and theme, and the Commercial Times (2023) also gives the host and chief curator; but the Reporter feature is output of one of the festival's own sub-projects and does not count as independent, and the edition numbering and level of resident participation remain unconfirmed, as noted (November 2026).

k46.name: Matsu International Art Island (ten-year ‘turning the soil’ art plan)
k46.creator: Lienchiang County Government (host); General Association of Chinese Culture (support); ‘Dapu plus+’ on Dongju (co-execution). First edition (2022) led by Wu Han-chung; third edition (2025) theme curator Nakaw Putun, with zone curators including Hung Yu-cheng, Huang Chen-yen and Kuo Mei-chun.
k46.place: The five islands of Lienchiang (Nangan, Beigan, Dongyin, Dongju, Xiju); sites include wartime strongpoints, bunkers, bomb shelters, harbours and village houses
k46.year: From 2022 (three editions held: 2022, 2023, 2025; planned by the county as a ten-year project)
k46.summary: A ten-year art project run by the Lienchiang County Government, inviting artists from Taiwan and abroad to place works in Matsu’s wartime strongpoints, bunkers, villages and maritime life, translating military spaces through local materials such as Matsu glass liquor bottles and marine debris. The first edition (2022, ‘Island Brewing’) had 41 teams and 39 works, with 50 Taiwanese volunteers on the ‘Island Return’ sub-project; the third (2025, ‘Paqiu — Your Ocean, My Land’) had over 50 works across three strands, plus ‘Ten People, Ten Seas’ co-created by local teachers and pupils with residents of Ogijima, Japan. Themes span the reuse of strongpoints after the lifting of military rule, everyday memory, Eastern Min language revival, depopulation and the marine environment.
k46.selfDesc: The Reporter (2024-08-03) notes the county, after military rule was lifted in 1992, drew on Matsu’s Eastern Min culture, wartime culture, baimei beliefs and ecology to launch the art island as a first step in cultural governance, aiming to stabilise tourism and train local talent; it also records that residents largely see the island as a channel for tourists and income rather than for art, that the promotion window is too short, and that one student said the art island ‘has not yet entered local people’s calendar’. Rti (2022) records the first edition led by Wu Han-chung, 41 teams, 39 works, 8 curatorial projects and 50 volunteers (part of the ‘Island Return’ sub-project). Artemperor records the 2025 third edition hosted by the county and the General Association of Chinese Culture, with multiple curators and over 50 works.
k46.pedagogicalInsight: This is the best case to discuss ‘how a large art festival relates to a place’ — not only the works, but the distance between the festival and residents. On the positive side it models using specific sites (bunkers, bomb shelters, harbours) and local materials (glass bottles, marine debris) as starting points, and ‘Ten People, Ten Seas’, which has primary-school teachers and pupils draw fish species together and co-create across islands with residents of Ogijima in Japan. But the resident distance recorded by The Reporter is teaching material too: with students or a workshop you can ask together ‘who is the festival really for’ and ‘what counts as bringing the local in, rather than using it as a backdrop’ — a counter-example to IBAE’s ‘start from context, not a preset theme’.
k46.why: Confirmed after your review (November 2026). Three independent outlets — The Reporter, Rti and Artemperor — agree on the host, curators, years and scale across three editions. Resident co-creation is moderately strong (there are concrete partners), but The Reporter also records residents’ distance, so both are kept.

k41.name: Chao Fangyuan: Seeing the Tidal Flats Art Festival (Ren Theatre's Fangyuan community theatre)
k41.creator: Fangyuan Township Office (host); Ren Theatre (operator, director Tsai Min-ni); Ren-ai community theatre (co-host)
k41.place: Fangyuan, Changhua (fishers’ plaza, tidal flats, mangrove sea-sky walk, Putian Temple)
k41.year: 2026 edition (Jul 26–Aug 1); the community theatre was formed in 2023
k41.summary: Ren Theatre’s director Tsai Min-ni proposed the Seeing the Tidal Flats incubation plan in 2022 and in 2023 formed a community theatre with the Fangyuan Ren-ai community association: fieldwork first, then collective improvisation with a dozen local non-professionals (including a 90-year-old and junior-high students) to turn fishing-village life, fishing songs and oral memory into theatre performed on the mudflats. The 2026 festival (Jul 26–Aug 1) ran four series on fishing-village memory and tidal-flat ecology.
k41.selfDesc: A 2025 feature by The Reporter says Tsai met documentary director Ke Chin-yuan in 2021, proposed the plan in 2022, and in 2023 formed the community theatre, completing Fangyuan, Our Home; she calls collective improvisation her working method, and the performers are a dozen locals of widely varying ages. A free drama class was expanded when sign-ups fell short. United Daily News (2026) reports the 2026 edition’s four series, a ‘tide banquet’ of 40 tables and 400+ guests, and that Ren Theatre has taken part for four years running.
k41.pedagogicalInsight: One of the fullest cases of ‘non-professionals making theatre’: the leader does not teach acting but uses collective improvisation so residents turn their own fishing-village life, songs and oral memory into a play. It models the full ‘fieldwork, then co-creation, no professional showcase’ flow, and how to put a 90-year-old and junior-high students on the same stage. Note: a free drama class had to widen recruitment when sign-ups fell short — a reminder that recruitment is itself part of participatory work.
k41.why: Confirmed as verified at your request (November 2026) on the strength of The Reporter’s independent feature plus United Daily News: the former confirms how the community theatre formed and who performed, the latter the scale of this edition.

k42.name: 2026 South-Link Art Festival: Flow of Mountain Trails
k42.creator: Taitung County Government (host); Dagedan Sea Travel (planning); curator Osan Karo; artists LUA RIVERA, basakanlan (Hsieh Cheng-yi), Wang Kuan-tung, Chen Sheng-chih
k42.place: Along the South-Link route in Daren, Jinfeng and Taimali, Taitung (Huayuan Elementary, Jialan, Jinlun Station, Laliba co-creation base and other communities)
k42.summary: A festival themed on the watershed invited four artist teams to survey the South-Link landscape through residencies and to live alongside local communities, with works sited at schools, train stations and a co-creation base. A satellite network of walks, workshops, lodgings and dining tables surrounds them.
k42.selfDesc: City.gvm (Global Views) reports each artist spent at least 12 days in residence, gathering fieldwork and living with residents across Indigenous, Hoklo, Hakka and foreign perspectives; Wang Kuan-tung did Paiwan fieldwork for his work. The festival also offered a limited ‘wave picnic box’ with local businesses.
k42.pedagogicalInsight: Artists creating through at least 12 days of residence, fieldwork and living with residents models a ‘live locally first, then create’ residency ethic; Wang’s Paiwan fieldwork is one route for an outside creator to enter Indigenous culture. Note: residents were mostly subjects of fieldwork, the degree of co-creation is not detailed, and there is clear tourism promotion — a chance to discuss with students where an art festival ends and tourism begins.
k42.why: Verified: City.gvm/Global Views (2026-08-22) and the Taitung County Government official page independently corroborate the core facts — the watershed concept, the four artists (LUA RIVERA, basakanlan/Hsieh Cheng-yi, Wang Kuan-tung, Chen Sheng-chih) and their four works and sites (THE ELDER at Huayuan Elementary, THE RESILIENCE OF LIFE at Jialan, COEXISTENCE CIRCLE at Jinlun Station, HOPE TAKES WING at Laliba), the run 1 Jul–31 Oct 2026, and the organiser (Taitung County Government) — so it is upgraded to verified. The planning team 'Dagedan Hailu' and curator Osan Karo still appear only in the original (unreadable) Hub News report, and residents actual role in creation is not detailed in any source. (daily source expansion, 2026-11-16)

k43.name: CTBC New Stage Arts Festival Charity Show: Puppet Theatre by Rural Schools
k43.creator: CTBC Cultural Foundation; Puppet & Its Double Theater (artistic director Cheng Chia-yin); teachers and students in Yilan and Gongliao (New Taipei)
k43.place: Yilan (Neicheng, Lize, Dongxing schools) and Gongliao, New Taipei (Gongliao Experimental Junior High); charity show at CTBC Financial Park, Taipei
k43.summary: Puppet & Its Double has long cultivated seed teachers in rural areas and led students to make puppet theatre. In the 2026 charity show, Neicheng students made The Mis-wished Wish — a story of over-wishing that leaves animals without water, until a small tree god grows — from their hometown’s tree god, earth god and water resources; Gongliao students took the Tamsui-Kavalan Trail as their theme.
k43.selfDesc: United Daily News (2026-09-14, Ho Ting-chao) says the show opened with a large puppet work co-produced by Puppet & Its Double and Japanese puppeteer Nori SAWA and combined stories by rural teachers and students; the winning schools included Lize, Dongxing and Neicheng in Yilan and Gongliao Experimental in New Taipei. The name ‘Dream Builder project’ appears in only one of the reports.
k43.pedagogicalInsight: A model of ‘seed teachers plus student creation’: the troupe trains teachers and guides students to turn their hometown’s faith (tree god, earth god) and water problems into their own puppet play, rather than performing for them. It shows how puppetry can let students handle an abstract ecological issue (over-wishing = water imbalance). Note: this is a corporate charity show, so the presentation carries corporate image and performance pressure, unlike an everyday classroom.
k43.why: Verified: the two original reports were from the same media group (UDN) and not independent; on 2026-11-19 two further sources independent of each other and of UDN were found — Liberty Times / art.ltn.com.tw (Tung Po-ting, 2026-09-14) and Commercial Times (Wang Tzu-ya, 2026-09-28) — both confirming the core facts: the CTBC Cultural Foundation's New Stage Arts Festival outdoor charity show on 2026-09-12 at CTBC Financial Park, with Puppet & Its Double leading teachers and students from four rural schools (Gongliao Experimental in New Taipei; Lize, Dongxing and Neicheng schools in Yilan) in co-created puppet plays; upgraded to verified. The headline puppet musical is named 'Play On! Good Earth Band' in the two independent reports (UDN's 'co-produced with Nori SAWA' framing stays single-source); the Neicheng play title 'The Mis-wished Wish' and the Gongliao theme (this entry's summary says the Tamsui-Kavalan Trail, but Liberty Times says Gongliao 'terraced paddies') remain to be checked. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-19)

k44.name: Making the Village Together: Zhongxing New Village Co-scene Action
k44.creator: Changhua County Cultural Affairs Bureau (host); sound artist Wu Hsiu-ming, artist Hsu Chia-chen, with the Muzhiyan team
k44.place: Zhongxing New Village (juan-cun) cultural park, Changhua
k44.summary: For public art at the Zhongxing military-dependents’ village park, the Changhua Cultural Affairs Bureau arranged a series of hands-on actions: sound-collecting and card-game workshops, timber construction, parent-child interactive theatre, VR and photography, aiming to turn a once-closed village site into an open public space.
k44.selfDesc: The source gives dates, workshop types, artists and host, but no attendance figures or outcomes.
k44.pedagogicalInsight: Opening a once-closed village site into a public space through many hands-on activities — sound-collecting, a card game, timber building — is a common ‘participation opens the site’ tactic in heritage activation, breaking one site into several low-barrier entry points (sound, play, timber, VR). But note: the source is a county-government advertorial the platform could not read directly, so the activities are a plan, with no independent evidence of real participation or outcomes — discount it as a teaching reference.
k44.why: Beyond the county-government advertorial (a CNA message-platform submission the platform originally could not read), two separately bylined reports from different outlets — Storm Media (Wang Hsiu-ho, 2026-05-01) and Yam News / GuanMedia Changhua (Chen Ya-fang, 2026-05-01) — now corroborate the host (Changhua Cultural Affairs Bureau), the artists (Wu Hsiu-ming's sound workshop, Hsu Chia-chen's card-game workshop, the Muzhiyan timber build) and the dates. But both quote the Bureau heavily and use county/Bureau-supplied images, sharing the same source as the original advertorial, so they are not independent corroboration and it stays to-be-verified. Attendance, whether former village residents co-created, and whether outcomes survive are still unsourced. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-17)

k45.name: 2026 Second Village Opens: Art, Dance, Memory — Echoes of the Unreturned
k45.creator: Yunlin County Government (host); TAMtamARTTAIWAN (planning); BIAU Dance Theatre (Barefoot Learning series); Huwei Jianguo Village Regeneration Association (operation)
k45.place: Jianguo military-dependents’ village, Huwei, Yunlin (Villages 1 and 2; bomb shelters, sentry posts, water towers and other military remains)
k45.year: 2026 (opens Oct 31, runs to Nov 1; originally Oct 24, postponed by a typhoon)
k45.summary: An art team and an international curator placed works inside the village’s bomb shelters, sentry posts and water towers, with dance workshops, talks and village tours to make village memory visible through contemporary art; the event also promoted the village’s food-farming and environmental-education direction.
k45.selfDesc: The Epoch Times report gives the curatorial team, sites, content and dates, and mentions ‘local participation’ but does not say how residents took part in curating or creating.
k45.pedagogicalInsight: Placing contemporary works straight into bomb shelters, sentry posts and water towers is a ‘the site itself is the gallery’ approach to heritage activation, so village memory is experienced through space rather than wall labels. For local-history teaching it models ‘let the historical site speak for itself’. Note: the source mentions ‘local participation’ but not how residents took part, so the real degree of co-creation is unclear; it is curation-led.
k45.why: Verified: beyond the user-supplied Epoch Times report (which the platform could not read directly), two independent bylined reports now corroborate the core facts — China Daily News (reporter Chen Cheng-fen, Yunlin, with her own on-site photos, 2026-10-31) and Taiwan News Net via Mediashi (reporter Li Wan-yu, 2026-10-31) — confirming the Yunlin County Government as host, the Jianguo Village Regeneration Association as operator, TAMtamARTTAIWAN as planner, BIAU Dance Theatre's 'Barefoot Learning', works set into the Villages 1-2 bomb shelters, sentry posts and water towers, and the Oct 31 and Nov 1 run; Taiwan News Net also confirms the original Oct 24 date was postponed by a typhoon. China Daily News is first-hand on-site reporting, so this is upgraded to verified. Whether residents co-created and the scale of participation are unstated in all three sources. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-17)

k40.name: Prototype Paradise
k40.creator: Prototype Paradise; lead artist Yoyo Kung; long-term collaborator Hsiao Yu-chin (per the Taitung County Government event page)
k40.place: Huannan Market, Taipei (2023) and the grounds of Taitung Art Museum (2023); the group's base is not stated in the reports
k40.year: From 2012 (began operating in 2012; the projects this platform could read date from 2015, 2023 and 2026)
k40.summary: Prototype Paradise is a contemporary performance group that formally began operating in 2012. Its core idea is "interacting with reality": performances happen in real spaces and invite people who are not professional artists to act as "experts of everyday life"; the group itself says what it does is closer to "disturbing" than "sourcing material". Its work is often built on interviews with vendors, sanitation workers, museum front-line staff and migrant workers; see the sub-projects below.
k40.selfDesc: A C-LAB interview (written by Hou Po-yen, 2022-11-10) says "experts of everyday life" is a term coined by Rimini Protokoll for laypeople who are neither professional artists nor real performers; as the creative party the group must take care not to disturb sanitation workers' work and invest in communication and safeguards so that everything happens with informed consent.

subs.n: Revisit Taitung Art Museum with Your Ears
subs.t: Two sessions on October 22, 2023 (10:30–11:30, 13:30–14:30) in the grounds of Taitung Art Museum, organised by Taitung County Government; instructors Yoyo Kung and Hsiao Yu-chin, co-creating teachers Yang Hui-ju and Chang Ling-yu, and 21 students. Graduates or students of Taitung Baosang Junior High served as "voice collectors", leading audiences around the grounds to hear their interviews with the museum's front-line staff; free, capped at 20 sign-ups. (From the Taitung County Government event page; the gap between 21 students and the cap of 20 is not explained.)

subs.n: Hundred Trades Scroll: Nightingales of Huannan
subs.t: One of four invited teams in "Huannan Table: 365 Days of Market Seasons" (May 20–Aug 6, 2023, Huannan Market; commissioned by Taipei's Market Administration Office and Department of Cultural Affairs, planned and run by the Chung Tai Foundation). After months of fieldwork and close interviews, the group explored vendors' subconscious images in fragmented sleep and turned their confessions into close-whisper sound theatre. (From Artemperor and CTWANT, which read alike and quote no vendors; the "18 months on site" refers to all four teams, while for Prototype Paradise only "months" is stated.)

subs.n: Following the Garbage Truck Around Taipei
subs.t: The group went out with sanitation workers along their routes, staging street performances and interactions, with a "story minibus" segment where veteran workers shared their experience. (From the C-LAB interview; routes, dates and partners could not be confirmed.)

subs.n: Walking Through Her Everyday Life: A Migrant Worker Dog-walking Sound Story
subs.t: Listed in the performance programme of the 2026 Taoyuan Iron Rose Art Festival, March 11–16, 2026, 19:00–21:00. (The festival page gives no venue, price, creative team, funders or description; the group's own site could not be read, so interview numbers, method and any later shows are not included.)

k40.pedagogicalInsight: this group spans the whole spectrum — the Taitung piece had teenagers act as ‘voice collectors’ interviewing on their own (facilitator-led), while Nightingales of Huannan had artists cut vendors’ confessions into sound theatre (artist-led). What is most worth learning is the ‘expert of everyday life’ stance: inviting non-artists as experts of their own field, not as amateurs. Informed consent and not disrupting participants’ work are also essentials of participatory practice.
k40.why: Verified: beyond the C-LAB interview, the international Institute for Public Art's case study independently documents Prototype Paradise's 'Travelling Around Taipei with Garbage Trucks' (2015), corroborating a curatorial team whose method combines performance, theatre, installation and public participation; PAR performing-arts magazine also carries Gong You-ying's writing on amateur participation. The group's existence and participatory method thus have two or more independent sources. Individual sub-projects vary in sourcing (the Taitung case is an organiser activity page, the Huannan case's two reports look like the same release, and the 2026 Taoyuan item gives only show times), as noted.

k38.name: Headwind Project (Chengcheng Junior High School)
k38.creator: Promoted by the Taiwan Good Foundation; supported by the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Justice; partners: Party Theatre troupe (drama) and Cloud Gate Dance School (martial arts and everyday movement); photo exhibition curator and photographer Lu Te-chen
k38.place: Chengcheng Junior High School, Hsinchu (a juvenile correctional school); the 2018 photo exhibition was at Zhongshan Underground Bookstreet, Taipei (Eslite R79)
k38.year: From 2017 (photo exhibition in Taipei from July 12, 2018; the Taiwan Good Foundation page gives Jul 12–30 without a year)
k38.summary: From 2017 the Taiwan Good Foundation has run the Headwind Project at Chengcheng Junior High School in Hsinchu, bringing art into a juvenile correctional school: a drama troupe leads interactive drama games, collecting stories from the boys' life experience and writing a play together; Cloud Gate's dance school leads martial arts and everyday movement to practise focus, endurance and bodily expression; and one class of boys spent about ten months recording themselves and each other on camera under curator Lu Te-chen. The results were shown in a photo exhibition at Zhongshan Underground Bookstreet in Taipei.
k38.selfDesc: CNA (2018-07-12) reports 15 students each in the drama and martial arts groups and a 30-boy class for the photo exhibition, co-organised by the Taiwan Good Foundation and Eslite. The foundation's page lists three exhibition themes: "Body Portraits", "Film Diaries" shot by the boys themselves, and "Dance Theatre" documenting the drama and dance workshops. The Initium (2018-11-03) calls Chengcheng the first juvenile correctional school in Taiwan to practise rehabilitative education and describes dance, drama and photography with dance showings and drama rehearsals.
k38.pedagogicalInsight: at a correctional school, drama, martial arts and image-making run in parallel — the play is written from the boys’ own life stories and the footage is shot by the boys themselves — giving ‘atypical’ students authorship is what is most worth borrowing. Note: the youths are minors in custody, so their privacy must be carefully protected in any presentation.
k38.why: Confirmed as verified at your request (November 2026). CNA and The Initium are independent news reports that agree on the Taiwan Good Foundation, the drama troupe, Cloud Gate's school and Chengcheng; the foundation's own page adds exhibition detail. The 2017 start rests on CNA alone for now.

k39.name: "Hearing the Voices of Along the River" Atypical Education Exhibition, National Palace Museum at Chengcheng Junior High School
k39.creator: National Palace Museum and the Agency of Corrections, Ministry of Justice (co-organisers); Chengcheng Junior High School (host/implementer); supporting: Heart Breakthrough Career Exploration Association and 104 Hope Foundation (per Commercial Times; the Epoch Times mentions only the former); art teachers not named
k39.place: Auditorium, 3rd floor of the administration building, Chengcheng Junior High School, Hsinchu County
k39.summary: The National Palace Museum's education team worked with Chengcheng teachers and students, and the results were shown in the school auditorium: replicas of museum objects, VR and film, plus student work in pastel, comics, Zentangle, LINE stickers, sculpture, DIY fabrication and songwriting, with students as guides. The Epoch Times says about nine months were spent teaching students the skills.
k39.selfDesc: The reports rely on the museum's statements and quote no students or teachers. The Commercial Times says the museum has trained juvenile inmates as guides since 2012; the Epoch Times says the museum has worked with seven correctional institutions including Taipei Prison since 2010 and does not mention 2012, so they may not describe the same thing.
k39.pedagogicalInsight: using Palace Museum works as a starting point and letting correctional-school students reinterpret them in pastel, comics, stickers and more, then guiding the tour themselves, models ‘taking high-barrier classics and designing low-barrier ways in’. Note: the reports read like a press release and do not detail how students took part in creating.
k39.why: Two outlets agree on dates, venue, the partnership and the content, but the pieces read like one press release with no teacher or student quotes; the "since 2012" claim appears only in the Commercial Times and differs from the Epoch Times' 2010.

k37.name: Yijia Art Museum (series)
k37.creator: Graduate Institute of Arts and Humanities Education team, Taipei National University of the Arts; partner: Taipei Honor Home for Veterans; course instructor and curator Wu Dai-rong (the page does not say whether the university is the organizer)
k37.place: Taipei Honor Home for Veterans (the Home of Righteous Soldiers); creation and exhibition take place in the residents' living space
k37.year: 2019 (the team entered the site in 2014 and a 2022 GPI review calls it eight years of interaction; since 2016 the project has used the name Yijia Art Museum, with a half-day show each International Museum Day; the 2019 show was on May 18)
k37.summary: From 2014 a team from Taipei National University of the Arts has worked at the Taipei Honor Home for Veterans, spending long periods with the Korean War anti-communist "righteous soldiers"; since 2016 the project has been called Yijia Art Museum and turns the soldiers' living space into a site for making and showing work. In 2019, the 65th anniversary of their arrival in Taiwan, it returned to the documents in the home's history room and asked how the word "freedom" was defined and used, and presented a half-day show on International Museum Day. A 2022 review on the GPI government publications site adds that the veterans moved from peripheral audience to participants in the co-creation, reflecting on freedom, nation, trauma and views of life and death from their own standpoint, and that an in-person show planned during the pandemic was turned into an online exhibition.
k37.selfDesc: The project website says the idea is to turn the home into an artistic eco-museum that values the process of making together over finished works, paired with an elective course. In 2019 the curatorial team reorganised the history room around a sentence on yellowed documents, "How to become a completely free person within 180 days!"; resident artists and teachers explored how freedom is represented and interpreted and invited participants to think together. The GPI review (Tseng Yi on Wu Dai-rong's book) adds that Wu developed an artist-teacher residency programme encouraging students to make site-specific work; participants include students, artist-teachers, and the veteran residents and administrative staff of the home; it describes the veterans as empowering themselves through art and becoming the creators.
k37.pedagogicalInsight: this project treats the teaching process itself as the art form, which makes it especially useful for anyone running long-term workshops. Methods worth borrowing: (1) start from found historical documents — the team began with a yellowed line in the home's history room, "How to become a completely free person within 180 days!", letting the large theme of "freedom" grow out of a real document rather than a teacher-set topic; (2) turn the site itself into a "conceptual eco-museum" — creating inside participants' own living space instead of a separate gallery; (3) value process over product — the review calls it "when teaching becomes form", with participants shifting from the observed to co-creators. A facilitator might ask: does my prompt emerge from participants' lives, or have I pre-set the answer? Note: how much say the veterans (participants) had in individual works is not detailed in the sources, so the actual degree of co-creation remains to be checked.
k37.why: Confirmed as verified after your review (November 2026). On Nov 3, 2026 a GPI review was added as a third source; it agrees with the team sites on the 2014 start, the International Museum Day shows and the partnership with the home, but it reviews the project leader's own book, so its independence is limited, and there is still no detail on individual veterans' participation.

k36.name: Pan-Austronesian Art Festival (Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts, 2021 Summer Exhibition)
k36.creator: Organized by Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts; director Lee Yu-ling as chief curator; New Zealand curatorial advisors Zara Stanhope and Reuben Friend; 23 artists and teams from Taiwan, Australia, New Zealand, Korea, Japan, Pakistan and France; architect Lu Chien-ming for the outdoor park
k36.place: Galleries of Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts, extending to the outdoor park around Neiwei Pond
k36.year: 2021 (Jul 17–Oct 31 per the museum's press release; overseas show in Washington, D.C., May 7–Jun 26, 2022)
k36.summary: The museum turned its 2021 summer exhibition into an international art festival centred on the ocean and islands, inviting over twenty artists to address Austronesian migration, cultural collisions of the Age of Discovery, and the traces of colonization and resource extraction, as well as encounters, collision and reconciliation among islands; it extends to the outdoor park around Neiwei Pond, where a water-system plant ecology restoration is under way.
k36.selfDesc: An interview on The News Lens says the three themes From the Known to the Unknown, Dark Islands and Cycles of Life correspond to encounter, collision and reconciliation, and the director stresses avoiding diversity with only "noise" and no "harmony". The curators began planning in 2019. The outdoor park takes drift-sea plants as its subject with an "organic landscape" concept; architect Lu Chien-ming led students of the Indigenous programme to tidy the park and restore plant diversity. Some artists (Laha Mebow, Chang Chih-chung, Jason Chiu and Margot Guillemot) represented Taiwan at the Jogja Biennale; four Taiwanese artists showed "Fluid Boundaries" in Washington in 2022.
k36.pedagogicalInsight: a large museum exhibition with weak community participation; what is useful is its thematic frame — encounter / collision / reconciliation to discuss Austronesian migration and colonisation, which can be borrowed to structure a lesson on Austronesian culture. Note: curation-led, not participatory.
k36.why: Verified: five sources agree on the organiser, chief curator Li Yu-lin, the 23 artist groups and the theme, and the museum's own opening release confirms the 17 Jul-31 Oct 2021 run and 62 works from 7 countries. Independent criticism is still thin, but the core facts are corroborated across the organiser's release and several reports.

k35.name: Interwoven Stories (Sadiljapan Old House, Tuban)
k35.creator: Curator tjuai (Chu Lien-hui); curatorial team not named in the report
k35.place: Sadiljapan old house, Tuban Village, Daren Township
k35.year: 2026 (reported Oct 29, "from today"; end date not mentioned)
k35.summary: The exhibition is held in an old house in Tuban Village, built around old objects kept in the house, which bring out the stories of Paiwan families and the community; the curator also speaks of craft, clothing and ritual contexts. The opening featured a tea gathering, guided tour and performance, and visitors shared how the stories moved them.
k35.selfDesc: The report says the exhibits include things left by a mother and tools the family used daily; the curator starts from the household collection to explore the objects' history and family stories, extending to Paiwan craft, clothing, rituals and history, so that people of different generations can learn about past life.
k35.pedagogicalInsight: using a mother’s belongings and everyday household tools from an old house as exhibits lets objects tell Paiwan family stories — ‘object-led storytelling’ suits schools, where one old thing can open a family-history lesson. Note: whether residents took part in curating is not reported; it is curation-led.
k35.why: Only one source (TITV), with promotional wording; awaiting your review. (Daily expansion, 2026-11-16: searched again for a second independent source but found only a different TITV exhibition and general Tuban travel/culture coverage — none corroborating this 'Interwoven Stories' Sadiljapan old-house show — so it stays pending with no source added.)

k32.name: 2026 Mattauw Land Art Festival: Meandering Zengwen River — the Inner Foothills
k32.creator: Chief curator Huang Ching-ying; 37 artists and teams from Taiwan, Japan, the Netherlands and elsewhere (41 works); source credited to Tainan City Government Cultural Affairs Bureau
k32.place: Seven zones: Zuoying Art Center in Madou (main venue), Zengwen Reservoir, Balin in Guantian, Paozailiao in Liujia, Zuozhen Old Street, Zhaoxing and Mizhi in Nanxi
k32.summary: The land art festival takes the highly meandering Zengwen River as its image and focuses on the foothill settlements upstream; artists went into settlements such as Paozailiao and Zhaoxing for residencies, did three years of fieldwork and interviews with "river guides", and raised public issues such as water resources and the "river-basin sacrifice system".
k32.selfDesc: The reports say preparation took three years and nearly half of the art projects went directly into foothill settlements. For example, singer Hsieh Ming-yu wrote the song "Yong-yong-a Huo" with local women of Paozailiao after long fieldwork and companionship, and Tsou hunter Basuya Agumang led Yu Hsin-lan and the Flying Squirrel Girls team on a flying squirrel survey. The festival raises "rights of nature" advocacy and the "river-basin sacrifice system" and plans an experimental "Nature Court"; it is described as Taiwan's first land art festival centred on a whole river basin and driven by advocacy.
k32.pedagogicalInsight: a singer co-writing a song with local women after long fieldwork, and a Tsou hunter leading a flying-squirrel survey, show the deep co-creation only possible when artists spend three years on site; the ‘watershed guide’ design is a good way to let locals be the guides. Note: for most sub-projects, how residents took part is not detailed.
k32.why: Four reports broadly agree on dates, zones, artist count and curators (one is a CNA wire report, one covers the Tainan City Government press conference), but all cover an official event with no independent review, the work count differs (41 vs 42) and the organizer is labelled inconsistently; awaiting your review.

k33.name: Art Heritage Community Story Co-creation: Elder Dance, Hakka Daily Life
k33.creator: Promoted by Hsinchu Living Aesthetics Center; Taichung-based Chi-Chih Physical Dance Company; residents of Douhuan Community, Toufen, Miaoli
k33.place: Presentation at the Tongluo Tea Factory of Taiwan Agriculture and Forestry Co., a Ministry of Culture "Top 100 Cultural Bases"; community: Douhuan, Toufen
k33.summary: The project began with exchange interviews and story collecting, then ran art workshops in which Douhuan residents and professional dancers turned family daily life, Hakka village life and plant-dyeing craft into a dance piece, presented at the Tongluo tea factory with residents and dancers on stage together.
k33.selfDesc: The report says the project is the 2026 edition of the "Art Heritage Community Story Co-creation Project" by Hsinchu Living Aesthetics Center, taking community plant-dyeing craft and Hakka life as material and weaving plant-dyed works, family daily life and community memory into the choreography; the dance company was founded in 1997. The center says it will continue the project.
k33.pedagogicalInsight: collecting stories through interviews, then putting residents on stage with professional dancers to turn daily life and plant-dyeing into dance — using the body and movement to handle ‘Hakka village life’ suits residents less at ease with words. Note: the number and age of residents and their role in decisions are not reported.
k33.why: Only the Hakka News (2026-09-07) source, which reads like a press release; awaiting your review. A 2026-11-15 search for additional independent coverage found none; held as pending. (daily source expansion, 2026-11-15)

k34.name: Meeting Places: Artist-in-Residence Co-creation (Taitung)
k34.creator: Organised by the Taitung County Cultural Affairs Dept. and Taitung Art Museum; local executing teams; resident artists and local venues across the years; project observer/critic Lu Pei-yi
k34.place: Local cultural venues and arts sites across Taitung (Chenggong, Zhiben, Changbin, Tjuwabar, Dawu, etc.)
k34.year: From 2021 (2021 Return: Rhythm of the Land; 2022 Return: Rhythm of the Sea; 2023 Re-Return; 2024 How to Bond; 2026 Undercurrent)
k34.summary: A Taitung artist-in-residence co-creation programme run by the county's Cultural Affairs Dept. and Taitung Art Museum since 2021. Unlike a conventional residency that removes the artist from their own environment, it has artists, local venues, residents and the environment meet and create as mutual subjects, while mapping local spaces, channelling resources to them and training local arts administrators. Each year takes a theme: 2021 'Return: Rhythm of the Land', 2022 'Return: Rhythm of the Sea', 2023 'Re-Return' (Tsai Kun-lin's sound-installation show 'Voices of Chenggong' at the Chenggong Indigenous Cultural Hall was one of that year's outcomes), 2024 'How to Bond' (three teams in residence for two months in Tjuwabar, Changbin and Zhiben), and 2026 'Undercurrent' (e.g. Juan Chung-kai's 'Corridor' in Dawu).
k34.selfDesc: An ARTouch Southern-Potential column by Lu Pei-yi (2024-12-06), writing as the project's observer, records the three 2024 'How to Bond' teams (Lai Yu-feng / Zhiben; Luo Yu-chi / Changbin; Chen Yu-chen & Li Pei-lun / Tjuwabar) and traces the 2021-2024 artists and venues; it invokes Wu Mali's 2006 'Tropic of Cancer Environmental Art Action' idea that 'artists become residents, residents become artists', explaining the programme's mutual-subject, process-over-product stance. Official pages of the Cultural Affairs Dept. and Taitung Art Museum, a book-launch page, Liang'an Haobao (2026 'Undercurrent'), and pages by the East Taiwan Research Association and Tjuwabar Time corroborate each year's residencies and showcases.
k34.pedagogicalInsight: The programme is itself a method of mutual-subject co-creation and a rich reference for educators: instead of removing artists from their environment, it has them meet and create with local venues, residents and place, with the local venue as the bridge between artist and community. Borrowable moves include pairing each artist with a local 'arts administrator' as bridge, a longer two-month residency that buys real relationships, and co-creation from locally grown material (a seed-paper workshop, rice-harvest shared meals). A caveat: the depth of 'co-creation' varies by year and team, so check who is actually creating when the word is used.
k34.why: Verified: the whole 'Meeting Places: Artist-in-Residence Co-creation' programme (Taitung, from 2021) is corroborated across several independent sources — Lu Pei-yi's ARTouch column (2024-12-06, independent observation/critique), Liang'an Haobao (2026 'Undercurrent') and Storm Media (2023 'Voices of Chenggong') — plus official pages of the Cultural Affairs Dept. and partner bodies. The single 2023 'Voices of Chenggong' show still rests on Storm Media plus the official page; 2024 'How to Bond' and 2026 'Undercurrent' rest on that year's sources. The Art Map piece is marked a Taitung County Government advertisement and is not counted as independent corroboration.

k01.name: Opening Gangshan: Boxes of Memory (Exhibition 2.0)
k01.creator: USR project team, College of Management, National Sun Yat-sen University; in cooperation with the Kaohsiung Museum of History
k01.place: Gangshan District (exhibited at the Kaohsiung Museum of History)
k01.summary:
This is a community art project in Gangshan, Kaohsiung, run by the USR team of the College of Management at National Sun Yat-sen University together with the Kaohsiung Museum of History.

The team invited Gangshan residents to start from their own memories and each make a “memory box”.

In 2023, 75 boxes were shown at the Kaohsiung Museum of History together with footage of the making process.
k01.selfDesc: The report says the project team and local residents made the boxes together, students inventoried the cultural resources of the old street, and elementary school teachers and pupils were among the creators. The exhibition also gave background on workshops about exploring the old street and discussing its future.
k01.pedagogicalInsight: This project shows how to turn the abstract theme of ‘local memory’ into a task anyone can do by hand; the techniques below can go straight into a classroom. Note: residents’ say over the wider curation is not reported, so the depth of co-creation is unconfirmed.
k01.why: Verified: besides the 1111 report on the 2.0 (2023) opening, Yam/今傳媒 (2022-06-16) reported the earlier 1.0 edition, corroborating residents making 'memory boxes' from their life stories and the Sun Yat-sen University-led co-creation method; the 1.0 co-organisers differ from the 2.0 (which involved the Museum of History), as noted.

k02.name: Ripples of Memory (Kaohsiung Gas Explosion Memorial Installation)
k02.creator: Artist Yen Ming-hung and team; organized by the Kaohsiung City Government Bureau of Cultural Affairs
k02.place: Intersection of Sanduo 2nd Road and Kaixuan 2nd Road (next to Wuquan Elementary School)
k02.summary: A public art installation commemorating the 2014 Kaohsiung gas explosions. Twisted metal pipes and broken pavement evoke the event, and "memory objects" provided by residents are embedded in the ground.
k02.selfDesc: The report says the selection process included community forums, briefings and in-depth interviews with residents, and residents' opinions were weighed in the jury's evaluation. Sixteen workshops were also held, with nearly 1,000 students from nearby schools. The work opened to the public in early July 2018.
k02.pedagogicalInsight: embedding residents’ ‘memory objects’ into an artist-led monument lets a community leave personal traces in a public memorial. For trauma topics it shows how physical objects can carry collective memory that is hard to put into words, rather than asking students to discuss disaster directly. Note: the balance between resident input and artist control is not reported.
k02.why: Verified: besides Storm Media, ARTouch (Hung Wei-che, 2018-07-09) describes this 'Ripples of Memory' land-art work in detail - the team Yen Ming-hung + Huang Ming-wei Architects, its five parts (Echo of Time, Walking Memory, Ripples, Pavement Landscape, and the participatory 'Overlap Box'), a prism refracting two rainbows daily 9:30-11:30 onto a memorial poem and the names of the 32 victims, and the choice of Wuquan Elementary (a forward command post after the blast); corroborated with Storm, it is upgraded to verified.

k03.name: Big Nose Youth · Dalinpu Memory Transit Project
k03.creator: Big Nose Youth (a local youth team; founder Cheng Tzu-ying)
k03.summary: Before relocation, a local youth team held community workshops where residents turned old protest banners into silkscreen works. The team also documented the neighborhood in short social-media videos.
k03.selfDesc: The report describes the team turning protest symbols into works of local memory, with residents taking part in the silkscreen printing. The background it gives includes disputes over industrial pollution and the relocation policy.
k03.pedagogicalInsight: reworking residents’ own protest banners — objects and history already in their lives — into prints is a clear ‘from context’ case: the issue is not handed down by the facilitator but grows from the community itself. The move of turning objects from a site of conflict into art is worth borrowing. Note: the workshop dates and scale are not reported.
k03.why: Verified: besides PTS (2025) on the community workshop turning protest banners into silkscreen prints, the Liberty Times (2026-11-08) reported the 'Big Nose Youth' memory-relay project in Dalinpu, corroborating the team and its pre-relocation memory-preservation work; the silkscreen workshop detail rests on PTS.

k04.name: Good Times Podcast (Dalinpu)
k04.creator: Hsu Jung-hung, Wu Yu-mei (a teacher at Fenglin Junior High School) and students
k04.summary: A junior high school teacher led students to interview the village head and elders, write scripts and draw a community map, producing a podcast about Dalinpu's food, beliefs and daily life.
k04.selfDesc: The report says students came to know their hometown anew and developed a sense of belonging, and that the program won a Golden Bell Award for Podcast Arts and Culture Program (the page does not state the year).
k04.pedagogicalInsight: a model case of ‘students as researchers’ — the teacher designs the interview–script–map–recording pipeline, and students go and interview elders themselves, so the themes (local food, faith, life) grow from their own fieldwork. It works as a cross-disciplinary project template. Note: whether students were co-creators or interview assistants is not reported.
k04.why: Pending: the 'Good Times' podcast made by a secondary-school teacher and students interviewing elders and village heads is mentioned only by PTS; no second independent source was found, so it is downgraded to pending.

k05.name: Jalan-Jalan: A Special Exhibition on Migrant Human Rights in Kaohsiung and Pingtung
k05.creator: Kaohsiung Museum of Labor; field research in cooperation with 1095 Studio for History and Culture
k05.place: Kaohsiung Museum of Labor (content covers four migrant living areas in Kaohsiung and Pingtung)
k05.summary: A special exhibition on the living landscapes of migrant workers and new immigrants in Kaohsiung and Pingtung. Field research came first; during the run there were Southeast Asian culture days, music performances and picture-book readings.
k05.selfDesc: The report says migrant workers and new immigrants were invited to take part: the opening featured a band of Southeast Asian migrant workers, new-immigrant groups shared life stories, and volunteers gave tours in Southeast Asian languages. The exhibition ran from December 26, 2021 to December 31, 2022.
k05.pedagogicalInsight: the show turns migrant workers and new residents from ‘objects on display’ into people telling their own stories — their own band, their own life stories, mother-tongue guided tours. For multicultural units the point is to let learners speak in their own language rather than be spoken for. Note: their role in curatorial decisions is not reported.
k05.why: Pending: this 'Jalan-Jalan' exhibition is reported under its name only by NOWnews; no second independent source naming this exhibition was found (nearby results are other Kaohsiung migrant events, not this show), so it is downgraded to pending.

k06.name: Lin Chun-yung Solo Exhibition: Black Surge
k06.creator: Lin Chun-yung (artist); curator Cheng Sheng-hua
k06.summary: A solo exhibition by Kaohsiung artist Lin Chun-yung. Using marine debris, tetrapods and the imagery of an industrial city, it looks back on Taiwan's ocean environment and industrial development, with 36 works on view.
k06.selfDesc: The report says the exhibition reflects on Kaohsiung's experience as an industrial and petrochemical hub, and takes the 2015 sperm whale stranding as the starting point for the marine-debris works. The Business Today report does not mention participation by residents or communities.
k06.pedagogicalInsight: this is a solo artist's work with no participatory element, but it works well as material for "look at the work, talk about transformation". A teacher could unpack how Lin Chun-yung turns marine debris and tetrapods — things usually treated as rubbish or background — into symbols of the industrial city and the sea, then ask students: is there something around you that everyone overlooks? The show was triggered by a 2015 sperm-whale stranding, which can prompt a discussion of how one concrete event becomes a starting point for making. Note: what this case teaches is how to read and borrow an artist's transformation, not how to run a participatory workshop — it is object-led, not process-led.
k06.why: Two independent reports agree on the exhibition's name and venue. The year is inferred from the publication dates.

k07.name: Zhongzhou Jinyu Festival
k07.creator: Faculty and students, Graduate Institute of Arts Management and Entrepreneurship, National Sun Yat-sen University; in cooperation with Tu Yi-wen (National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University)
k07.year: From the first edition in 2021 (dates for 2.0 not mentioned)
k07.summary: A community arts festival in Zhongzhou, Cijin, with installations, guided tours, workshops and lectures, plus a local publication, Jinzhou Journal, compiled from local history materials.
k07.selfDesc: The report says a community long-term care center took part in making works, residents joined in a dance piece and video documentation, and it mentions background such as pollution from Kaohsiung Port and shipbuilding, relocation, the decline of fishing-port culture and an aging community.
k07.pedagogicalInsight: a ‘community art festival plus a local journal’ gathers scattered local history into something exhibitable and readable, with care-centre elders taking part too. It shows how to round off oral and image collecting into a publication. Note: residents’ role in the curation is not reported.
k07.why: Verified: besides the 1111 report, Bo News (Li Chih-wen) independently covered the Zhongzhou Jinyu Festival, corroborating the Sun Yat-sen University arts-management institute as founder, the installations at Zhongzhou on Qijin, the tours/workshops/talks and the Jinzhou journal.

k08.name: Kaohsiung Military Dependents' Village Trilogy
k08.creator: Hou Shu-tzu (video artist)
k08.place: Villages in Zuoying; Huangpu New Village, Fengshan
k08.summary: Over about eight years the artist visited military dependents' villages in Zuoying and Fengshan, using residents' oral accounts and video to record daily life and memories of displacement during redevelopment and demolition.
k08.selfDesc: The report is an excerpt from The Long Day Wanes, built around the oral account of one elderly woman, Grandma Liu, whom the author interviewed several times and invited back to her village. The trilogy comprises We Meet Here, The Long Day Wanes and Where Is Home.
k08.pedagogicalInsight: this is an artist’s eight-year solo project; residents are interviewees, not co-creators. It shows how long companionship plus oral history and images build a trustworthy record of a place — the key is repeated return visits and relationship-building, not one-off collecting. Note: it is object-led, not a participatory workshop.
k08.why: Verified: besides the Storm book excerpt, the VT Artsalon solo show 'The Long Day Closes' (2015) corroborates Hou Shur-tzy documenting, through images and residents' oral accounts, the lives of military-dependent households in Fongshan's Huangpu Village after they moved out, and the village's demolition, consistent with the 'Kaohsiung Military Village Trilogy' (a different show and outlet).

k09.name: Mudan Forest–Village–Sea Environmental Art and Design Camp
k09.creator: Department of Craft and Creative Design, National University of Kaohsiung; co-organized by Mudan Township Office and Mudan Township Community Development Association; in cooperation with Cheng Shiu University
k09.place: Xuhai, Mudan Township, Pingtung (Mudan Bay section of the Langqiao–Beinan Historic Trail)
k09.summary: University faculty and students worked with tribal residents to make three installations from driftwood and discarded fishing nets, on themes of ethnic integration and marine waste, and developed an AR application to present past years' works.
k09.selfDesc: The report says resident Pan Kun-lin taught students to weave discarded fishing nets, and a Mudan Township Office section chief said the camp has trained more than 15 amateur artists from the tribe.
k09.pedagogicalInsight: the roles flip here — instead of artists teaching residents, a community member (Pan Kun-lin) teaches university students to weave discarded fishing nets. It shows how ‘letting locals be the teachers’ brings learners into a place’s context. Note: residents’ role in choosing the themes is not reported.
k09.why: Pending: the Mudan 'Forest-Village-Sea' environmental art camp has only the 1111 campus-news source; other results are either the same outlet's university news or other Mudan projects, and one Liberty Times piece could not be read, so it is downgraded to pending.

k10.name: Street Museum (first edition: Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District)
k10.creator: Taipei Fine Arts Museum; in cooperation with Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District
k10.place: 228 Memorial Museum (results exhibition); Zhongqin Village, Zhongzheng District
k10.summary: The Taipei Fine Arts Museum worked with residents, inviting 34 senior villagers to gather local memories and create works starting from paintings in the museum's collection. The results were shown alongside collection pieces.
k10.selfDesc: The report says the project plans to expand to Taipei's 12 districts year by year, with goals including participation by older adults, intergenerational dialogue and local identity. The exhibition ran from December 21, 2019 to March 22, 2020.
k10.pedagogicalInsight: using a museum painting as a starting point gives elders a concrete way in, then asks them to gather their own memories to create — a neat way to lower the barrier for first-time makers. For senior groups it shows how one existing work can draw out personal memory. Note: the media of residents’ works are not described.
k10.why: Verified: besides Taiwan News, 1% STYLE (LINE TODAY, 2025) also refers to the Taipei Fine Arts Museum's Zhongqin-li edition of 'Street Corner Museum' and its method of using collection paintings to prompt elders' local memories; note that piece dates the Zhongqin-li edition to 2019 (this entry says 2020), so fieldwork and the formal show may fall in different years.

k11.name: Turning Around in the Old City (Street Museum 2024)
k11.creator: Taipei Fine Arts Museum; artists Hsu Chia-chen, Tsui Kuang-yu and Lung Sze-liang
k11.place: Zhongshan Hall (border of Zhongzheng and Wanhua districts)
k11.summary: Centered on everyday memories of Ximending and Chengzhong Market, the project held an old-photo card-game workshop and a phone-video workshop, inviting residents and local shopkeepers to create together.
k11.selfDesc: The report says local merchants, residents and artists took part in creating the work, with the artists acting as "counselors."
k11.pedagogicalInsight: the artists call themselves ‘facilitators’ rather than creators — the stance itself is a model, using low-barrier tools like an old-photo card game and phone video so residents and shopkeepers tell their own stories. Both workshop formats are directly reusable.
k11.why: Verified: besides Islands of Museums, Mirror Media (2025-01-13) independently covered the 2024 'Street Corner Museum: City Turn', corroborating the Taipei Fine Arts Museum as host, the Chengzhong district/market theme and the card-game workshop made from shopkeepers' memory objects; the phone-video workshop detail rests on Islands of Museums.

k12.name: Freedom of Movement: Encountering the Last Scenes of Ankang Public Housing (Xinglong Social Housing Public Art Project)
k12.creator: Tomorrow Studio; artists Chen Po-yi, Fengjing Yinghua Creative Society, Liu Yi-yin and others
k12.place: Three vacant units in Ankang Public Housing, Wenshan District
k12.summary: Before residents moved out, three vacant units were turned into an exhibition combining residents' calligraphy, restored old photographs, plaster hand casts and a documentary, showing their different choices about "movement" and "home."
k12.selfDesc: The report says Tomorrow Studio's "Xinglong Living Room" had been on site for over a year, holding baking, drawing and small-trip activities. Residents took part in the key-visual collage and contributed personal objects and stories.
k12.pedagogicalInsight: the ‘Xinglong Living Room’ spent over a year on cookie-baking, drawing and small trips to build relationships before making an exhibition — showing the ‘befriend first, create later’ rhythm of participatory work. It is a reminder for rushed workshops that relationships take time. Note: residents’ role in decisions is not reported.
k12.why: Verified: besides Islands of Museums, CNA (2024-03-21) reported the 'Freedom to Move' public-art show for the Xinglong social housing, corroborating an exhibition before the Ankang relocation, curation by Tomorrow Studio, and residents' stories shown via the documentary 'Monologue of Ruins'; items such as calligraphy, plaster hand-casts and photo restoration rest on Islands of Museums.

k13.name: We Are Home: Guangci Social Housing Public Art Project
k13.creator: Participating artists include Hsu Yung-hsu, Chiu Cheng-hung, Tseng Ling-li and Peng Kuan-chieh (the organizer's report does not state this explicitly)
k13.place: Guangci Social Housing complex, Xinyi District
k13.summary: A social-housing public art project built on long-running series of workshops (private kitchen, book and recipe swaps, social prescriptions) and 18 installations to build relationships among residents.
k13.selfDesc: The report lists a private-kitchen project for women's center clients, herbal healing and a community garden, a community flag made together by residents, and works drawn from the dreams of more than ten residents told in interviews.
k13.pedagogicalInsight: using everyday ongoing activities — shared kitchens, book-and-recipe swaps, ‘social prescriptions’ — as the medium lets residents build relationships before any artwork. It shows a community art project can begin from something as ordinary as eating together and swapping recipes.
k13.why: Verified: besides Yahoo/Yam, CNA (2025-01-10) reported the 'We Are Home' public-art results show for the Guangci social housing, corroborating the site, curation by He Lei Art (Wu Hui-chen), 18 installations plus the 'Museum of Migration', over 200 community workshops before the show, and residents' stories as material; specific strands such as the private kitchen, book/recipe swaps and 'social prescriptions' rest on the original report.

k14.name: Sundays Unseen: One-Forty International Migrant Photography Award Exhibition
k14.creator: National Theater & Concert Hall "2026 Autumn Arts Festival" and the One-Forty International Migrant Photography Award; migrant worker photographers from Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand working in Taiwan
k14.place: Gate 2, National Theater (21-1 Zhongshan S. Rd., Taipei)
k14.summary: An exhibition of photographs that migrant workers in Taiwan made with phones or cameras of their own lives. The photographers decide what to shoot and how they want to be understood; the show starts from the question "what if you had only one day off a month?" and is free to visit.
k14.selfDesc: The report says the award has run since 2019, 2026 is its seventh edition, it is based on Photovoice theory, and this is its first showing at the National Theater & Concert Hall. The show presents the 2026 winners and selections from past years, with entries from migrant workers from Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand; it has three sections (Limited Space | Survival Mission, Limited Time | Relaxing the Mind, Limited Self | Becoming Yourself), covers labor, diaspora, identity and memory, and ends with a reading list on migrant-worker issues. Open daily 12:00–20:00.
k14.pedagogicalInsight: a model Photovoice case — migrant workers decide what to shoot and how they want to be seen, with the award giving only a frame and a prompt (if you had one day off a month). For teachers who want learners to hold the narrative, it is the cleanest template: the facilitator poses the question, participants answer it themselves.
k14.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). A LINE TODAY report and Marie Claire both mention the NTCH–One-Forty collaboration, but the dates, venue and edition number still rest on one source; the Vogue and NCAF pages could not be read.

k15.name: "Cool Symbiosis" Gender Exhibition
k15.creator: Museum of National Taipei University of Education; 11 artists and groups including Liu Yu and Lee Mao Huan
k15.place: Museum of National Taipei University of Education
k15.summary: Eleven groups of artists collaborated with scientists and other practitioners, using stories of biological and gender diversity to help audiences understand and accept sexual minorities.
k15.selfDesc: The report says the exhibition hopes audiences will come to see the diversity of biology and gender.
k15.pedagogicalInsight: no community participation — this is an issue exhibition meant to help audiences ‘understand and accept’. But it models a strategy of using ‘biodiversity’ as an analogy for ‘gender diversity’, placing a sensitive topic in more neutral scientific language — one way in for gender discussions. Note: it is curation-led, not participatory.
k15.why: Verified: besides PTS, Taiwan News reported the MoNTUE show 'Queer-Symbiosis' with 11 artist groups, and the Taiwan Contemporary Art Archive and C-LAB magazine also document it, so the core (MoNTUE, 11 groups, gender/biodiversity themes) is corroborated across sources.

k16.name: ADAM Artists' Laboratory
k16.creator: Taipei Performing Arts Center (curator River Lin); 2019: 12 artists from 12 countries; 2026: 7 artists from Indonesia, Vietnam, Hong Kong, the Philippines, Australia, Japan and Taiwan
k16.place: 2019: Longshan Temple area in Wanhua and Dadaocheng Theater; 2026: Manila (August residency) and Taipei (October residency and meeting)
k16.summary: ADAM (Asia Discovers Asia Meeting for Contemporary Performance) is an international artist residency and exchange platform run by Taipei Performing Arts Center since 2017. In 2019 (3rd edition) 12 international artists spent about four weeks in Taipei visiting LGBTQ, migrant worker, homeless and Indigenous communities before presenting and exchanging at the annual meeting; the 2026 edition (9th) is a Manila–Taipei two-city residency themed "Holding Situationships".
k16.selfDesc: The 2019 report says the theme was "Community (and) Art", concerning the social turn in contemporary art; the residency began July 22 for four weeks and the annual meeting ran August 15–18. The 2026 official pages say the 9th edition is held every two years (since 2025) with three strands (Artist Lab, New Work Exploration, Exchange & Forum), runs October 15–18, uses the concept of "Laundry Days", and includes city walks in Taipei (Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, National Palace Museum, Shung Ye Museum of Formosan Aborigines, Machangding Memorial Park, etc.).
k16.pedagogicalInsight: this is an international residency and exchange platform for artists; communities are visited and met, not co-creators, so its direct classroom value is limited — more an administrative model for designing residencies. Note: in 2019 artists visited and exchanged with communities rather than co-creating.
k16.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). The 2019 year and third-edition status are corroborated by Taiwan News and a Global Gender report; the 2026 edition is described by Taipei Performing Arts Center and National Performing Arts Center pages, which differ slightly in detail.

k17.name: "Interwoven": Co-creating the Museo Aero Solar
k17.creator: New Taipei City Museum of Art; artist Tomás Saraceno; a community college linking schools and community groups in the Sanying–Tushu area
k17.place: New Taipei City Museum of Art (Yingge District)
k17.summary: Members of the public collectively collaged and painted recycled plastic bags to help make the floating sculpture Museo Aero Solar, which rises on solar heat; the museum also held a lift-off experiment, and the work was shown in the exhibition "Interwoven".
k17.selfDesc: The report says the project has developed since 2007 and been carried out in more than 30 countries, and that this is its first time in Taiwan. The museum's page calls it an important extension of the exhibition, combining artistic creation, environmental thinking and public participation; exhibition coverage says the work belongs to the artist's Aerocene project, and the Taiwan version includes works by Taiwanese participants and results from earlier showings in Thailand and Korea.
k17.pedagogicalInsight: ‘open-source, everyone builds one big thing that flies’ is a low-barrier, high-reward way to draw participation. But the editNote notes it is the Taiwan version of an international project, with a theme (environmental sustainability) that does not grow from local life — against IBAE’s ‘from context’, it is a ‘content-first’ example, useful as a counter-case.
k17.why: Previously confirmed by human review (October 2026). The newly added museum page, Marie Claire, Yam and the international project page agree on the work's name, exhibition dates, citizen co-creation and the project's 2007 origin; no source describes the Taiwan co-creation process in detail.

k18.name: The Futurists: Living Practices for Future Cities
k18.creator: Curated by Haobanshe; 9 artists and groups including Wei Chao-yi, Liu Kai-chen, Chang Cheng-chun, Hsu Chia-chen and Wei Theatre
k18.place: Beitun Social Housing; Wuqi Sanmin Social Housing
k18.summary: Public art shown in social housing: residents contributed old photos and life stories, a theater workshop invited them to talk about "moving house," and spaces normally closed to the public, such as rooftops and mailbox areas, were opened.
k18.selfDesc: This is a critical essay by a curator. The author questions measuring community empowerment by KPIs and asks what the public art will leave residents after the project ends.
k18.pedagogicalInsight: the source here is a curator’s critique that asks exactly the question educators should — once the project ends and the KPIs are stripped away, what does the public art leave residents? It is a reminder not to treat ‘how many events, how many attendees’ as proof of empowerment.
k18.why: Confirmed: besides The Reporter's on-site critique, an official Taichung City (Housing Development Engineering Office) news release (2025-10-18) and the Artemperor exhibition page independently corroborate the core facts — organized by the Taichung City Housing Development Engineering Office, curated and run by Haobanshe, shown at Beitun and Wuqi Sanmin social housing, 17-26 Oct 2025, 9 artists/groups, with artists doing prior in-residence fieldwork — matching The Reporter, so it is upgraded to confirmed. The resident-participation details (old photos and life stories, a theater/script-reading workshop on 'moving house', opening rooftops and mailbox areas) still rest mainly on The Reporter alone. (Daily source expansion, 2026-11-14)

k19.name: Bu Long Project (Open, and next Art Experiment Field)
k19.creator: Indigenous Peoples Cultural Foundation (organizer); Taoyuan City Indigenous Peoples Affairs Dept. (partner); KIRI Indigenous Peoples Cultural and Creative Park (co-organizer); artists Ali Istanda (Hu Chia-yu), Siyat Moses (Juan Yuan-min) and maya' a taboeh hayawan (Luo Yuan)
k19.place: KIRI Indigenous Peoples Cultural and Creative Park, Qingpu (Zhongli and Dayuan districts, Taoyuan)
k19.year: 2026 (official page: 1 Jul–31 Aug; earlier reports: residency Jun–Aug, Taiwan Design Expo in September)
k19.summary: Three young Indigenous artists in residence in Qingpu used local materials such as irrigation ponds, temple incense ash and fallen leaves to run free participatory workshops recalling pond memories lost to development; the official programme also includes a "Qingpu Sensory Archive" city-exploration activity visiting old settlements, ponds and Laojie River.
